Depiction, interpretation, and what opens it

nodes_added.body:
## Depiction, interpretation, and what opens it **DEPICTS** names the artifact's objective contents — one edge per thing shown, medium-neutral: a song depicts a horn as surely as a picture does. Depiction claims confirm at the gate; a depicted thing canon does not know is a gate question with two recorded answers — create the citizen here, or ignore it with an [Approved Omission] so a re-scan never re-asks. What the artifact STANDS FOR is an **[Interpretation]**: one per intent, ABOUT exactly one artifact, INTERPRETED_AS its subject, DRAWS_ON only things the artifact depicts. The objective layer and the meaning layer stay separate on purpose — two worlds may read the same picture differently without contesting what it shows. A **[Resolver]** binds a scheme and a location kind to what knows how to open it — OPENS_WITH exactly one [Procedure] or [Citizen Bookmark], so "how do I open this kind of thing?" is canon, not folklore. And an artifact that replaces another says so: the newer SUPERSEDES the older, and the older carries when it was superseded — the marker is the model's; what a world does about what still cites the older one is that world's reading. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["[Artifact]
identity: its name
grade: content held"] N["a newer [Artifact]"] L1["[File Location]
scheme - address - primary
verified fingerprint - sequence - size"] L2["another location kind
rests unverified by design"] T["a thing it shows"] S["what it stands for"] I["[Interpretation]
one per intent"] R["[Resolver]
scheme + location kind"] P["[Procedure] or [Citizen Bookmark]"] A -- LOCATED_AT --> L1 A -- LOCATED_AT --> L2 A -- DEPICTS --> T I -- ABOUT --> A I -- INTERPRETED_AS --> S I -- DRAWS_ON --> T R -- OPENS_WITH --> P N -- SUPERSEDES --> A ```

nodes_added: Identity is the name; location is a row

nodes_added.body:
## Identity is the name; location is a row

An **[Artifact]** is the thing itself, as canon knows it: its identity
is its NAME — a stable handle in the world's own words — never a path.
WHERE it is lives on **[Artifact Location]** rows behind LOCATED_AT,
each carrying a scheme, an address, and whether it is the primary
copy; an artifact has exactly one primary. Copies move, get renamed,
appear in second places; the artifact stays one citizen and its
locations are rows that come and go.

**[File Location]** is the kernel's own location kind — the one the
engine natively resolves, reads, and verifies. A world may declare
further location kinds under [Artifact Location] through the ordinary
taxonomy ceremony; a location of a kind the engine cannot read rests
unverified by design, stated plainly rather than guessed at.

## Parked, by name

Named here so absence never reads as oversight: **Transcribed** as an
artifact grade (content carried at region grain, with receipts);
a kernel location kind for the web (an https scheme with its own
verification story) and, with it, the resolver's OPENING VERB — today
a [Resolver] names what opens a location kind, and nothing yet turns
that key; and the conversion of the engine's own records' citations
into located artifacts, awaiting the web location kind. Each arrives,
if it arrives, through its own gated design dialogue — parking is
sequencing on evidence, never a quiet no.

# The artifact model — identity, location, meaning

The things a person hands a world — a picture, a song, a rulebook, a
spreadsheet — become citizens, and this record tells that model whole
as it shipped: what an artifact IS (identity), where it can be found
(locations, with verification the machine's own fact), how much of its
content canon actually holds (the grade), what it objectively shows
(depiction), what it stands for to this world (interpretation), and
what knows how to open it (resolvers). The design was settled in owner
dialogue and landed with the kernel ceremony that promoted [Artifact]
and its family; the parked remainders are named at the end.

nodes_added: The grade is the content held

nodes_added.body:
## The grade is the content held

How much of the artifact's content canon holds is the artifact's
grade — the kernel's Completeness ladder applied as CONTENT HELD, on
the same KNOWN_AT edge every graded citizen carries. **Cited**: canon
holds the name and where to find it, nothing more. **Attested**: canon
also holds a description and its confirmed DEPICTS facts — enough to
reason about the artifact without opening it. **Transcribed** — the
content itself carried at region grain, with receipts — is designed
and parked; no shipped machinery claims it.

The grade is about CONTENT, deliberately: whether the bytes at a
location are really there and really unchanged is a different kind of
fact, and it never folds into the grade.

nodes_added: Verification is the location row's own fact

nodes_added.body:
## Verification is the location row's own fact

What the engine actually read is stamped where the reading happened:
on the location row. At apply, every file location of every artifact
the round touched is read and stamped — `verified_fingerprint`,
`verified_at_sequence`, `size` — and a file location that cannot be
read refuses the round, collated, before anything is written. The
receipts sweep reads the same rows later, so "is the file still what
canon verified?" is a query, never a memory.

A non-text artifact (an image, a PDF, audio) enters at its **floor
receipt**: `python -m graph receipt <file>` prints the fingerprint,
size, and the medium the bytes declare, and the comprehension room
refuses to read it for structure plainly, receipt in hand — what the
engine cannot comprehend it still identifies, and silence never reads
as held.

Artifact-hood follows the taxonomy: a citizen whose kind descends from
[Artifact] is an artifact to every rule here — the gate, the stamp,
and the sweep all fold the kinds. Citations resolve among artifact
kinds first, and a citation the machinery can no longer resolve is an
ERROR by name, never a silently dropped connection.
